adults.title: Close to Jesus Christ, and Bringing Someone Along
adults.big_idea: A desire to be close to Jesus Christ is what makes a missionary, and each of us can help someone, especially in the rising generation, take the next step toward serving Him.
adults.objective: Learners will name one person they can encourage toward the Savior or toward missionary service and choose one specific thing to do for that person this week.
prepare: Read Bishop Douglas's talk, especially the story of Elder Merlin Sanchez (paragraphs 8–12).
Read Mosiah 28:3 and Doctrine and Covenants 31:1, 3, 5–7.
Bring a slip of paper and a pencil for each person.
Write two headings on the board: What friends and leaders did / What the Lord did.

segments.name: Who helped you?
steps: Begin with prayer. If you wish, sing or read the words of Called to Serve.
Ask the first question below and give ten seconds of quiet before anyone answers.
Have learners turn to one person and share for one minute each. Invite two people to tell the whole group what their helper actually did.
Explain that Bishop Douglas, of the Presiding Bishopric, spoke mainly to missionaries and to the rising generation. Today we will ask what his message asks of the rest of us.
questions: Think of someone who helped you, or someone you love, come closer to Jesus Christ. What did that person actually do?

segments.name: What makes a missionary
steps: Tell how Bishop Douglas watched his two great-nephews, who are brothers, speak in sacrament meeting before leaving for missions thousands of miles from home, and how they reminded him of the sons of Mosiah.
Ask someone to read Mosiah 28:3 aloud while the others listen for what the sons of Mosiah could not bear.
Read the key quote from paragraph 6 about their desire, then President Nelson's words that Bishop Douglas quoted.
Discuss the questions. Let learners carry the conversation; add only what is needed.
questions: Bishop Douglas names what takes a back seat for a season: education, dating, careers, family time. When has putting the Lord first for a season blessed you or someone you know?
Where have you seen that kind of desire in a missionary, young or senior?

segments.name: The story of Elder Sanchez
steps: Form groups of three or four. Ask each group to read paragraphs 8–12 of the talk on a phone, or read them aloud to the class if phones are few.
As they read, have groups list on paper everything that friends and leaders did and everything the Lord did.

Gather the lists on the board under the two headings. Be sure these details appear: a faithful friend helped Merlin begin his mission papers and schedule a physical exam before he had decided to serve; friends and leaders helped him return to church at age 25; the Lord removed obstacles one by one once he decided to go.
Read aloud Merlin's answer when Bishop Douglas asked why he wanted to serve (key quote from paragraph 9).
Point out what followed: he was called as a bishop on his wedding day and now serves as a stake president. Read the key quote from paragraph 11 about lifelong discipleship.
questions: The friend acted before Merlin had decided. What does that teach you about how to help someone without pushing?
Who is doing the most in this story: Merlin, his friends, or the Lord? What makes you say so?

segments.name: What the Lord promises those He sends
steps: Explain that Bishop Douglas closed with the Savior's words to Thomas B. Marsh, called to preach in 1830, and invited the rising generation to put their own names in place of Thomas's.
Invite everyone to read Doctrine and Covenants 31:1, 3, 5–7 silently and mark each promise the Lord makes.
Ask learners to call out the promises they found and write them on the board.
Read President Oaks's words from the start of the talk (aligned quote), then Elder Dube's invitation from this conference (aligned quote). Note that Elder Dube's invitation is to us all.
questions: Which of these promises would a young person you love most need to hear right now? Why?
Which promise speaks to a worry you carry about your own family or your own ability to share the gospel?

segments.name: One name, one step
steps: Hand out the slips of paper. Allow two full minutes of silence.

Ask each person to write one name: a young person preparing for a mission, a new convert, someone who has stopped participating, or a missionary now serving. If the Spirit suggests their own name, for a senior or service mission, they may write that.
Under the name, have them write one thing they will do this week. Offer the ideas in the Act list if anyone is stuck.
Invite one or two volunteers to share the step they chose, without sharing the name.

segments.name: Witness and follow-up
steps: Read the key quote from paragraph 15 about room and a special place. Bear a brief testimony that the Savior does open hearts, as He promised Thomas: “I will open the hearts of the people, and they will receive you.”
Tell the class you will begin next week by asking two or three people what happened when they acted. Make a note to do it.
Close with prayer.

key_quotes.text: Their desire to serve the Lord rose above every other personal ambition.
I only want to be close to Jesus Christ and to follow Him.
serving a mission is just one of many significant steps on the path of lifelong discipleship.
There is still plenty of room and a special place reserved for each one of you!

scriptures.use: Read aloud in segment 2. Listen for what the sons of Mosiah could not bear, then ask where learners have seen that same desire.
Read silently in segment 4. Mark every promise the Lord makes to the one He sends, then list the promises on the board.
Optional, if time allows in segment 3: read Amulek's words and ask how a patient friend can help someone who has been called many times and has not yet heard.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Dallin H. Oaks
aligned_quotes.text: We invite all [of God’s children] to come unto Christ by repentance and baptism and confirmation in order to open the doors of the celestial kingdom to the sons and daughters of God. No one else can do this.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Dube
aligned_quotes.text: My humble invitation to us all: Will you find one person and invite him or her to come unto Christ by exercising faith to follow His teachings, or invite a friend to meet with the missionaries?

takeaways: A desire to be close to Jesus Christ is what makes a missionary.
A faithful friend can take a practical step with someone before that person has decided.
The Lord opens hearts and removes obstacles for those who choose to serve Him.
act: Do one practical thing for the person whose name you wrote: offer a ride, sit with them at church, or help with one step of mission preparation they have been putting off.
Write or message a missionary now serving and tell them one specific way their example strengthens you.
Tell a young person or a new convert, in a sentence or two, why you want to be close to Jesus Christ.
Pray by name for one young person in your ward or family who is deciding about a mission, and for the missionaries serving where you live.
adapt: At home with adults: skip the small groups. Read paragraphs 8–12 aloud together, make the two lists on one sheet of paper, and keep it where you will see it this week.
Short on time: do segments 1, 3 and 5 only (about 16 minutes).
Large class: have groups work on the two lists at their seats and ask only three groups to report.

youth.title: Put Your Name in the Verse
youth.big_idea: God prepared you to invite His children to come unto Christ, and the Savior's call to serve is addressed to you by name.
youth.objective: Youth will decide where a mission belongs on their own list of plans and choose one step of preparation to take this week.
prepare: Read Bishop Douglas's talk and Doctrine and Covenants 31:1, 3, 5–7.
Bring a slip of paper and a pencil for each person.
Write the six scrambled story lines from segment 3 on the board and cover them until you need them.
Label four corners of the room, on paper or just by pointing: Education, Dating, Family time, Sleeping in.
Ask youth to bring scriptures or phones; they will use them.

segments.name: Top five
steps: As youth sit down, hand each a slip and a pencil. Say: You have sixty seconds. Write the top five things you hope to do in the next ten years. Go.
Call time. Ask them to put a star by the one that matters most and keep the slip face down. No one has to share.
Offer a prayer, or ask a youth to. Say that Bishop Douglas of the Presiding Bishopric spoke straight to the rising generation, and today they get to answer him.

segments.name: What takes a back seat
steps: Explain that Bishop Douglas listed things that take a back seat for a season on a mission, including education, dating, careers, family time, and sleeping in on Saturday mornings.
Say: Walk to the corner that would be hardest for you to set aside. Ask one person in each corner for a one-sentence reason.
While they are still standing, have someone read Mosiah 28:3 from a phone, then read President Nelson's words that Bishop Douglas quoted (aligned quote).
Have them sit and discuss the questions.
questions: Bishop Douglas says the Lord's expectations are high and that it is worth it. What would make it worth it to you?
What did the sons of Mosiah want so much that everything else could wait?

segments.name: Story scramble: Elder Sanchez
steps: Split into two or three teams. Uncover the board: (A) Called as a bishop on his wedding day. (B) A friend helps him start his mission papers. (C) Baptized at nearly 24. (D) A desire to serve suddenly swells in his heart. (E) Serves as a missionary in Lima, Peru. (F) Stops participating for a time.
Teams race to put the letters in order using paragraphs 8–11 of the talk on their phones. First team with the right order (C, F, B, D, E, A) and able to point to where the talk says so wins.
Ask a youth to read aloud what Merlin said when asked why he wanted to serve (key quote from paragraph 9).
Add the ending: today Merlin is a stake president, and he and his wife, Gali, have three children. They cannot fathom what their lives would be if he had not served.
Discuss the questions.
questions: The friend helped with mission papers before Merlin had decided. Who has done something like that for you, or who could you do it for?
Merlin's reason was not about where he would go or what he would get. What do you notice about his reason?

segments.name: Honest questions
steps: Say: Here are questions people your age really ask. What if I am not sure I want to go? What if I do not know enough? Is it the same for young women and young men? Let them add their own.

Read paragraph 14 of the talk together. Be clear and gentle about what the prophets have said: the Lord has asked every worthy, able young man to prepare for and serve, and for him it is a priesthood responsibility; for young and able sisters a mission is a powerful, but optional, opportunity, and they are invited to pray to know if the Lord would have them serve.
Read Alma 10:6 and ask what Amulek admits about himself. Point out that Bishop Douglas said some might be like Amulek, and that Merlin's story shows it is not too late to hear.

For the worry about not knowing enough, read paragraph 16: Bishop Douglas says they already have a testimony of Jesus Christ and His Atonement that can bless the world. Then read Elder Caussé's words about testimony (aligned quote).
Read the key quote from paragraph 7 about being held in reserve. Ask the question below.
questions: Bishop Douglas says, “Take care not to become distracted.” What are the alternatives of far less worth that could quietly crowd a mission off someone's list?

segments.name: Your name in the verse
steps: Read the second invitation in the Invitations list: Bishop Douglas invited each of them to put their own name in place of Thomas's.
Have everyone open Doctrine and Covenants 31:1, 3, 5–7 on a phone or in their scriptures. Give three minutes of real silence to read it with their own name in verse 1.
Ask them to copy onto the back of their slip the one phrase that felt most like it was meant for them.
Invite a few to share their phrase and why. Do not press anyone.
Point out the promises attached to the call, such as “your tongue shall be loosed” and “I will open the hearts of the people, and they will receive you.”
questions: How did it feel to read these verses with your name in them?

segments.name: Back to the list
steps: Read the first invitation in the Invitations list word for word.
Have youth turn their slip over to their top five. Silently, they decide where a mission belongs on that list and write it there. For young women, that may mean writing: pray to know.
Ask each to circle one step from the Act list, or write their own, to do before next class.
Bear a short testimony of the Savior and of the truth that they are needed. Tell them you will open next week by asking who took their step and what happened. Close with prayer.

key_quotes.text: God held you in reserve for this time.
I only want to be close to Jesus Christ and to follow Him.
Don’t be distracted by alternatives of far less worth.
Lift up your heart and rejoice, for the hour of your mission is come

scriptures.use: Read aloud in segment 2 while youth stand in their corners. Ask what the sons of Mosiah wanted so much that everything else could wait.
Read in segment 4. Ask what Amulek admits about himself and how Merlin's story shows it is not too late to hear.
Read silently in segment 5 with your own name in place of Thomas's. Copy one phrase onto your slip.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Russell M. Nelson
aligned_quotes.text: Nothing else compares in magnitude, nothing else compares in importance, nothing else compares in majesty.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Caussé
aligned_quotes.text: It need not be long, eloquent, or dramatic—it only needs to be true.

invitations.text: To all the rising generation of the Church, I invite you to place serving a full-time mission high on your list.
I invite each of you to substitute your name for Thomas’s

takeaways: God prepared me, before I was born, to invite His children to come unto Christ.
The best reason to serve is wanting to be close to Jesus Christ and to follow Him.
The Lord's call comes with promises, and I can read them with my name in them.
act: Pray this week to know what the Lord would have you do about a mission, and write down any thought or feeling that comes.
Read Doctrine and Covenants 31:1, 3, 5–7 once more at home with your name in it, and put your phrase where you will see it every day.
Ask a returned missionary one honest question: What was hard, and why was it worth it?
Be the faithful friend: do one practical thing to help a friend come to church, a class, or an activity.
adapt: At home or with two or three youth: skip the corners and teams. Talk through what would be hardest to set aside, order the story lines together, and spend the saved time on Doctrine and Covenants 31.
Short on time: do segments 1, 5 and 6 (about 12 minutes) and tell Merlin's story in a few sentences.
If recent converts or youth who are unsure about serving are present, let Merlin's story lead: he was baptized at nearly 24 and had not planned on a mission.

children.title: I Can Share the Good News of Jesus
children.big_idea: Jesus wants everyone to know about Him, and I can help by sharing His good news and being a good friend.
children.objective: Children will say that they can share the good news of Jesus and will choose one way to do it this week.
prepare: Bring a flashlight and a small blanket or towel.
Bring a soft ball, plus paper and crayons for each child.
Be ready to tell the story of Elder Sanchez in your own simple words (see segment 3).
Practice the three hand actions: hands on heart (love), hands held out (share), a wave toward yourself (invite).

segments.name: Good news
steps: Sing I Hope They Call Me on a Mission, then have a child offer a prayer.
Ask the question below and let several children answer.
Say: The very best news is about Jesus. Today we will learn how we can share it. Teach the truth for today and say it together twice: I can share the good news of Jesus.
questions: What is some good news you were excited to tell someone?

segments.name: The flashlight
steps: Dim the lights a little. Turn on the flashlight and cover it with the blanket. Ask: Can the light help anyone now?
Let a child pull the blanket off. Ask what changed. Remind children never to shine the light in anyone's eyes.

Explain that a leader named Bishop Douglas spoke at general conference to missionaries and to young people getting ready to be missionaries. He said missionaries radiate the Light of Christ. We do not hide that light. We share it.
Pass the flashlight around the circle, pointing it at the ceiling. Each child who holds it says one thing they know about Jesus. Help anyone who is stuck: Jesus loves me. Jesus helps me.
Say the truth together again: I can share the good news of Jesus.

segments.name: Act out the story of Elder Sanchez
steps: Have everyone stand. Tell the story in short parts, and have the children do each action with you.

Say: A man named Merlin was baptized. (Hands on heart.) For a while he stopped coming to church. (Sit down.) A good friend helped him. (Reach out a hand and help a neighbor stand.) Merlin came back to church. (Walk in place.)
Say: Then Merlin wanted very much to be a missionary. Bishop Douglas asked him why. Merlin said he only wanted to be close to Jesus Christ and to follow Him. (Hands on heart.)

Say: Merlin became a missionary in a country called Peru and told many people about Jesus. (March in place.) Today he is a father and still helps many people come to Jesus. (Wave toward yourself, as if inviting.)
Ask the questions below.
questions: Why did Merlin want to be a missionary?

segments.name: Roll the ball
steps: Sit in a circle. Tell the children that in the Book of Mormon the sons of Mosiah wanted everyone to hear about Jesus. If a child can read, have them read Mosiah 28:3 aloud; otherwise tell it in a sentence.
Roll the ball to a child. That child tells one way to be a good friend like the friend who helped Merlin, or one thing they could tell someone about Jesus. Then they roll it to someone new.
Keep going until every child has had a turn. Praise each answer.
End with everyone standing and saying the truth once more.

segments.name: Draw and put your name in
steps: Explain that long ago Jesus called a man named Thomas to share the gospel, and told him to be happy about it. Bishop Douglas invited those he was speaking to to put their own names where Thomas's name is.
Give out paper and crayons. Help each child write their name at the top, followed by the Savior's words from the talk: “Lift up your heart and rejoice.”
Ask children to draw themselves sharing the good news of Jesus or being a helping friend.
Walk around and ask each child to tell you about their picture.

segments.name: Love, share, invite
steps: Read Elder Stevenson's words from this conference (aligned quote) or simply say his three words: love, share, and invite. Teach the three hand actions and do them together twice, a little faster each time.
Practice in pairs. One child pretends to be a friend; the other practices saying something kind and inviting them to play, to Primary, or to hear a favorite story about Jesus. Then switch.
Ask each child to pick one thing they will do this week: say something kind, share their picture with someone, or tell someone one thing they know about Jesus.

segments.name: Sing and witness
steps: Sing I Want to Be a Missionary Now.
Tell the children in one or two sentences that you know Jesus loves them and that Bishop Douglas said, “We need you!” Say the truth together one last time.
Tell them you will ask next week who they shared with. Close with prayer.

key_quotes.text: I only want to be close to Jesus Christ and to follow Him.
You are not only the messengers but also living examples of the message.
Lift up your heart and rejoice

scriptures.use: In segment 4, have an older child read it aloud, or tell it simply: the sons of Mosiah wanted everyone to hear about Jesus.
In segment 5, tell children that Jesus told Thomas to be happy about sharing the gospel. Children write their own name with the words Lift up your heart and rejoice.
Optional for older children: read it together and ask what Jesus asked His disciples to do and what He promised them.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Stevenson
aligned_quotes.text: I invite you to do something that is as simple as gospel fruit is delicious: love, share, and invite.

takeaways: Jesus wants everyone to know about Him.
A good friend helps others come to Jesus.
I can share the good news of Jesus now.
act: Show your picture to someone and tell them what it means.
Say something kind to a child who is alone and invite them to play.
Tell someone one thing you know about Jesus.
Pray for the missionaries by name if you know one.
music: I Hope They Call Me on a Mission
I Want to Be a Missionary Now

adapt.younger: For ages 3–7, shorten the ball game and the drawing by a minute or two each and repeat the story actions a second time instead. Write each child's name and the words on the paper for them, let helpers take turns holding the flashlight and the ball, and say the truth for today after every activity.
adapt.older: For ages 8–11, have a child read Mosiah 28:3 and another read Matthew 28:19–20, and let an older child lead the story actions. Ask a harder question: Merlin's friend helped before Merlin had decided to serve; why do you think that mattered? Invite them to write one sentence of what they know about Jesus under their drawing.
